editorNote: This week's papers lean on cost questions: when extra inference compute is worth it, how to scale a distillation critic, and how to train steadier reasoners. All claims come from the arXiv abstracts.

stories.headline: Looping a trained model pays for its extra compute only at small scale, a Qwen study finds
stories.summary: Across Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 models from 0.8B to 9B parameters, adding loops after training beat both baselines only for the 0.8B model; at 4B and 9B it failed to beat an equal-parameter model.
stories.whyItMatters: For post-hoc looping, the authors conclude it pays off only for small models with a fixed parameter budget.

sourceLinks.title: There Is No Free Loop: When Does Looping a Trained Model Pay for Its Inference Compute?

stories.headline: Zyphra's hierarchical attention builds a tree over the KV cache for subquadratic long-context attention
stories.summary: ZHA routes queries top-down through a tree of compressed key summaries, and can be applied to pretrained models with a short KL distillation over a few billion tokens while keeping long-context retrieval, reasoning, math and agentic coding performance.
stories.whyItMatters: The authors' performance model suggests large gains beyond 1M tokens of context; that is a model-based projection, not a measured result.

sourceLinks.title: Subquadratic Attention with a Hierarchical Tree-Structured Indexer

stories.headline: CRoS rewards reasoning models for depending on step order, lifting out-of-domain accuracy and faithfulness
stories.summary: Shuffling reasoning steps without changing their content gives a causal-reliance reward; with Gemma-3-4B on Reasoning Gym it reaches 46.8% on five unseen datasets versus 43.8% for the best baseline, and 34.0% hint acknowledgment versus 20.2%.
stories.whyItMatters: It targets a weakness of answer-only RLVR rewards, though results are on one 4B model.

sourceLinks.title: CRoS: Causality Reward on Scrambled CoTs Improves Accuracy and Reasoning Faithfulness

stories.headline: Joint scaling of critic and teacher, plus a step-aware critic, stabilizes few-step distillation
stories.summary: In Distribution Matching Distillation, a larger teacher with a small fixed critic can lower student quality and cause collapse; growing the critic with the teacher prevented that, and a step-aware critic (STAC) further helps across ImageNet, SDXL, FLUX.2 and Wan2.1.
stories.whyItMatters: It gives a concrete recipe for scaling DMD teachers without training collapse.

sourceLinks.title: A Better Critic Matters for Distribution Matching Distillation

stories.headline: Exact worst-case analysis gives optimal, monotonically decreasing SGD stepsizes for smooth convex problems
stories.summary: For dimension d ≥ N+1, the paper gives an exact worst-case analysis of the final iterate over any N stepsizes in [0, 1.5]^N; when the variance bound is at least Ω(1/√N), the minimax-optimal schedule is unique and decreasing.
stories.whyItMatters: The decreasing optimum rules out acceleration from fixed fractal schedules of the kind seen in the deterministic case.

sourceLinks.title: Exact Theory and Optimal Stepsizes for Stochastic Gradient Descent in Smooth Convex Minimization

stories.headline: Stochastic environments can speed up plasticity loss in RL, and TD instability takes over in the hardest settings
stories.summary: Training SAC on three DeepMind Control tasks with controlled noise, plasticity-preserving methods improved robustness on the two harder tasks; resets plus layer normalization underperformed resets alone at every noise level tested.
stories.whyItMatters: In the most challenging settings the authors find TD instability, not gradual plasticity loss, is the main failure mode.

sourceLinks.title: Towards Understanding the Impact of Plasticity Loss on Reinforcement Learning in Stochastic Environments
